summary: Gate 2 candidate adds only packaging-validation.json plus its SHA256SUMS line; no other package content changed. The receipt is internally consistent with the checkout: it names the gate 1 commit 5183e2d07 as preparation_commit, its embedded verifier result (630 files, 624 byte-preserved, 1171 source entries, manifest 1433a210...) matches verify_archive.py's return shape and the current manifest.json checksum; its 629 payload_hashes equal the pre-receipt SHA256SUMS content and spot-checked entries (FINAL_REPORT.txt, SOURCE_SHA256SUMS, archive-map.json, report .md) match current SHA256SUMS lines. Current SHA256SUMS has 630 entries (631 package files including itself) and includes the receipt, so the receipt is checksum-bound and the verifier's exact-coverage rule would reject its removal or alteration. The recorded git diff --name-only output lists only the three package roots and correctly excludes the receipt (taken pre-receipt). Whitespace exclusions, hook exceptions, 30 Python files and 2 shell files match the README and the actual tree. Verifier logic is read-only and the five tamper subcases cover modified, missing, extra, symlink and SHA256SUMS-refreshed-but-map-mismatched cases. Limitations in the receipt, README and report are honest and mutually consistent (no event-array replay, derived storage summaries, sizing hash index, no reruns/C1/Run77). Three nonblocking advisories: the deferred G2-PYCACHE-COVERAGE, semantic checks lacking negative full-copy tests, and the receipt not being referenced from README/report. No new blocker found.

findings.evidence: package_files() uses rglob('*') over SCRIPTS and EVIDENCE and verify() requires set(checksums) == all files, so any __pycache__/*.pyc created by running the verifier or tests without python -B causes 'Checksum coverage differs'. README line 72-73 documents -B; receipt argv includes -B; no bytecode present at this checkout.
findings.requested_change: Deferred per agreed scope; nonblocking. Optional future hardening: ignore __pycache__ directories in package_files() or state the failure mode explicitly in the README.

findings.evidence: All five full-copy tamper subcases fail at the checksum/coverage/mapped-hash stage (lines 57-63 of verify_archive.py) before any semantic check runs. The approval binding, sample-contract, pair-order, CSV, median, sustained and storage checks (verify_archive.py lines 74-189) are exercised only positively via test_complete_archive; only near() has a unit-level negative test.
findings.requested_change: Nonblocking advisory for a follow-up commit: add at least one tamper subcase that refreshes SHA256SUMS, archive-map.json and SOURCE_SHA256SUMS consistently after mutating a derived value (e.g. campaign-summary.json median) and asserts the semantic error string, so the data-consistency layer is proven to reject drift independently of the checksum layer.

findings.evidence: Neither the README 'Offline verification of this package' section nor the report's 'Evidence and scripts' list (pr299_perlmutter_20261115.md lines 161-177) mentions packaging-validation.json, and grep for the file name in both returns nothing. The receipt is self-describing and checksum-bound, but a reader has no pointer to it or to its pre-receipt payload scope.
findings.requested_change: Nonblocking: in a later documentation commit, add one sentence to the README verification section (and optionally the report evidence list) naming packaging-validation.json as the validation receipt and noting that its archive_result and payload_hashes describe the pre-receipt 630-file payload.
